publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: French Students Protest Over Education Funding Shortages
cards.content: Tensions are running high in France as thousands of students protest against education funding shortages and job prospects, with hundreds of new demonstrations announced across the country. The protests are expected to be joined by workers' unions and key figures from the yellow vest movement, with calls for a new system to address France's financial woes. Economist Anne-Laure Delatte believes that France needs constitutional change to overcome its financial challenges, while centrist politician Anne-Catherine Loisier thinks that the protesting students must feel heard and that local governments can make improvements by redistributing funding better.

cards.title: Russia Returns Ukrainian Asylum Seekers to Moscow
cards.content: Russians who fled their country after the Ukraine invasion and sought asylum in the US or Europe are now being forcibly returned to Russia, amid a growing trend of deportations. Katya, one such deportee, was denied asylum in the US and forcibly returned to Moscow, where she was interrogated by Russian security services. cards.title: Ukraine liberates 277 sq km in Donbas, inflicts heavy losses on Russia
cards.content: Ukraine has made gains in the Donbas region, liberating 277 sq km and inflicting heavy losses on Russia. Ukrainian drones led the assault, and Russian drones threatened soldiers. Despite Russian airstrikes, Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi has been successful, with 8,000 Russian casualties and few Ukrainian losses. The operation was aided by Elon Musk's Starlink satellite communications network, but restrictions imposed without warning have sparked concern. Ukrainian soldiers are celebrating their gains and look to the future, while relations with Washington are strained due to differing views on Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Star Feeds on Brown Dwarf in Rare Cosmic System
cards.content: Astronomers have discovered a unique cosmic system where a small star, 300 light-years from Earth, is slowly eating its companion, a brown dwarf. The star and brown dwarf are remarkably close, with the brown dwarf's entire orbit fitting within the Sun's diameter. The star is feeding off the brown dwarf's material, a process that could last billions of years. This is the first observation of a low-mass star consuming material from another low-mass object.

cards.title: Astronomers Find First Green-Colored White Dwarf Star
cards.content: Astronomers found a white dwarf star that would appear green to human eyes, a first. The star's color is caused by the interaction between helium and other elements in its atmosphere, which can reveal clues about planetary material and how planets formed.

cards.title: Species Losses Erode Ecosystem Benefits, Study Finds
cards.content: A new global study suggests that losing species can steadily erode the benefits ecosystems provide, including pollination, clean water, and natural pest control. The research, led by King's College London and Imperial College London, found that ecosystems have less spare capacity than previously assumed, meaning that species losses could have significant consequences for the environment and climate. The study's findings also highlight the importance of protecting marine life, as it plays a crucial role in capturing and storing atmospheric carbon dioxide.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Vanilla Compound Found to Help Wounds Heal
cards.content: Researchers at Flinders University have found that vanillin, the compound behind vanilla's sweet aroma, has antibacterial and antioxidant properties that could be used to help wounds heal. Vanillin is a low-cost and abundant ingredient that could be used to create wound-care materials and deliver drugs, making it a promising candidate for biomedical applications.

cards.title: Ear Device Controls High Blood Pressure in Severe Cases
cards.content: a small ear stimulation device tested by researchers at Queen Mary University of London showed promise in controlling high blood pressure that persists despite medication. The device, which delivers gentle electrical pulses through the ear, was found to be safe and practical to use at home. While it did not significantly lower blood pressure overall, a subgroup analysis found that those with more severe hypertension saw a greater reduction in blood pressure using the device.

cards.title: Blueberry Powder May Help Mild Depression in Older Adults
cards.content: A small study found that older adults with mild depression who consumed daily blueberry powder had a greater reduction in symptoms than those given a placebo, but the difference was not statistically significant. The study also found subtle changes in the gut microbiome, with the fiber and dark pigments in blueberries potentially modifying the gut microbes and their products, which could be relevant to depression.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Deforestation Rate Falls 15% in 2025, Shortfall Persists
cards.content: The world's deforestation rate declined by 15% in 2025 to seven million hectares, but it's still far from meeting its goal of halting deforestation by 2030. The Forest Declaration Assessment 2026 found that despite the decline, the world has accumulated a 10.7 million hectare deforestation reduction shortfall since 2021. Tropical Latin America and the Caribbean reduced deforestation, while forest loss continued to rise in tropical Africa. Forest protection and restoration received only 0.3% of global climate finance in 2024.

cards.title: India hit by heavy rainfall, orange alerts issued
cards.content: India faces heavy rainfall, with orange alerts issued for Tamil Nadu and South Interior Karnataka. Southern states are likely to experience intense rainfall, flash floods, and waterlogging, while other regions may see thunderstorms and strong winds. Delhi and surrounding areas can expect cloudy skies, light showers, and gusty winds, with temperatures ranging from 18 to 31 degrees Celsius. The weather department has warned of lightning and winds reaching 40-50 kmph, advising residents to be cautious and avoid flooded areas.

cards.title: Floating solar farms expand renewable energy production
cards.content: Floating solar installations are becoming an increasingly attractive option for regions where land is limited. Panels installed on reservoirs and other water bodies can generate electricity while reducing pressure on valuable land resources.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Global film festivals spotlight a new generation of filmmakers
cards.content: Film festivals around the world are giving greater attention to emerging directors and independent productions. Organisers say new filmmakers are experimenting with storytelling techniques and technologies while exploring social and cultural themes.

cards.title: New stadium technology changes how fans experience live sports
cards.content: Sports venues are adopting larger digital displays, real-time statistics and connected services to create more interactive experiences for spectators. The technology is also helping teams analyse matches and improve stadium operations.

cards.title: Music platforms experiment with new ways for artists to reach audiences
cards.content: Music platforms are experimenting with new discovery tools, personalised recommendations and direct connections between artists and listeners. The changes are reshaping how new musicians build audiences and release their work.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Record 12 Ships Attacked in Strait of Hormuz in One Week
cards.content: The number of ships attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz has reached a record high, with 12 vessels hit in the last week alone. This surge in attacks has slowed the recovery in oil shipments through the strait, industry data suggests. The attacks are part of Iran's efforts to assert control over the waterway, experts say.

cards.title: UK Chancellor Plans Tax Hike on Banks to Boost Revenue
cards.content: UK Chancellor John Healey is planning to increase taxes on the bank sector, with possible options including reversing a 2023 reduction in the bank surcharge or raising the bank levy. Bank shares fell on expectations of a tax hike, with Lloyds and NatWest dropping over 2%. Some experts argue that banks, which made £15bn in profit in the first half of the year, should contribute more to the government's budget. Healey praised the role banks play in the UK economy, but trade unions and some experts call for a fairer share of taxes from the sector.

cards.title: Small businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence tools
cards.content: Small businesses are adopting AI tools for customer support, marketing, document processing and data analysis. Lower-cost AI services are making technologies that were previously available mainly to large companies more accessible to smaller firms.
